source.title: Representation of manipulable man-made objects in the dorsal stream

confidence_rationale: Simply viewing or naming pictures of tools, but not other object categories, selectively activates left ventral premotor cortex (putative human homologue of canonical F5 grasp neurons) and left posterior parietal cortex (akin to monkey AIP). Object identity and associated action knowledge are therefore neurally co-represented for tools. Held at 0.48: correlational fMRI, category-level (tool vs non-tool) rather than token-level binding, and an early small-sample study.
failure_signatures: The object->action link is expressed at the CATEGORY level (tools as a class recruit premotor/parietal action regions) -- evidence for type-keyed affordance knowledge, which is not the token-instance object-file binding ARC-082 places at V4; the two may need to coexist.

Activation during passive viewing and naming is correlational; it does not show the premotor/parietal activity is used for object recognition or action selection, so it cannot by itself distinguish a bound object->action representation from associative co-activation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: fMRI during viewing and naming of pictures of tools versus other object categories showed that tools selectively activated left ventral premotor cortex (BA 6) and left posterior parietal cortex (BA 40). The authors relate these to monkey canonical F5 and anterior intraparietal neurons that respond to graspable objects without movement, and propose a close link between manipulable objects and information about the actions associated with their use.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports ARC-082's premise that tools are a specialisation in which object representation and afforded action are tightly linked: recognising a tool engages the motor representations of its use even without acting. In REE this is the biological motivation for folding the SD-016 cue->action pathway into the object representation (ARC-080) instead of keeping a standalone projection.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Early blocked-design fMRI with a small sample; category-level contrast (tools vs animals/houses/faces), not token identity; correlational. It evidences type-keyed action knowledge, whereas ARC-082's V4 endpoint is token-keyed. Human cortical dorsal-stream anatomy has no direct analogue in the V3 substrate; transfer is at the level of 'object and action share a representation'.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI; passive viewing and silent naming of pictures of tools and other object categories; frontal and parietal regions of interest.

confidence_components.notes: Influential and broadly replicated finding (tool-selective premotor/parietal responses), but this specific study is small, early and correlational. Mapping moderate-low because it is category-level rather than token-level object->action binding.
